new_task_1.title: Use finite default widths when plot size or linewidth data is constant
new_task_1.description: Plot normalization now handles constant-valued size and linewidth encodings without dividing by zero. When all mapped values are identical, xarray assigns a stable default width instead of producing invalid normalized widths.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray plotting APIs that map data values into marker sizes or line widths still produce usable widths when the mapped data is constant rather than varying.

expectation.grounded: The plotting normalization helper must accept width ranges with an explicit default value `(min, default, max)` and, when the input data has `max == min`, return that default width for every element instead of normalizing by a zero range. The built-in marker-size range should use `(18.0, 36.0, 72.0)` and the built-in line-width range should use `(1.5, 1.5, 6.0)`.
expectation.conceptual: Plots that encode a variable into visual width should remain renderable even when that variable is constant. A no-variation input should map to a sensible default appearance rather than yielding invalid or undefined widths.

constraints.grounded: For non-constant data, width normalization must continue to scale linearly between the configured minimum and maximum widths. The change should only alter the constant-data case by substituting the configured default width, without changing how interval handling or other plotting-type validation works.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the fix narrowly scoped to the degenerate normalization case. Existing width scaling for varying data should remain intact, while constant-value plots become deterministic and safe.

behavior: Plot width normalization now uses a three-part width range of `(min, default, max)` instead of only `(min, max)`.
When all values used for marker-size scaling are identical, every plotted element receives the default marker width rather than an invalid normalized width.
When all values used for line-width scaling are identical, every plotted element receives the default line width rather than an invalid normalized width.
When mapped values vary, normalized widths continue to interpolate between the configured minimum and maximum bounds.
acceptance_criteria: When a user creates an xarray plot whose marker sizes are derived from a constant-valued data variable, the plot should render with finite marker sizes for every point instead of producing invalid widths from zero-range normalization.
When a user creates an xarray plot whose line widths are derived from a constant-valued data variable, the rendered widths should remain finite and equal to the configured default width.
When a user plots varying size or linewidth data, the resulting widths should still scale across the configured minimum-to-maximum range rather than collapsing to the default width.
When the mapped width input is constant zero or any other constant value, the observable result should be the same stable default-width rendering rather than a special-case failure.
